Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 62, verses 1–4:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Yusabbihu lillahi ma fi al-samawati wa ma fi al-ard﴾: That is, whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of all created beings glorifies (yunazzihu) God, exalted is He, above whatever is unbefitting to Him, by the tongue of speech and the tongue of state. He did not say "man" (من) instead of "ma" (ما), giving precedence to the non-rational (ghayr al-'aqil) because of its abundance over the rational (al-'aqil).

﴿Fi al-ummiyyin﴾: That is, the Arabs, because of the rarity of those among them who could read and write.

﴿Rasulan minhum﴾: That is, Muhammad (ﷺ), since he is Arab, Qurashi, Hashimi.

﴿Wa yuzakkihim﴾: That is, purifies them in spirit and in character.

﴿Wa yu'allimuhum al-kitaba wal-hikmah﴾: That is, the guidance of the Book and the secrets of its guidance.

﴿Wa in kanu min qablu lafi dalalin mubin﴾: That is, and indeed they were, before the mission of the Messenger, in the error of polytheism and jahiliyyah.

﴿Wa akharina minhum lamma yalhaqu bihim﴾: That is, and [He sent him to] others of them, believing righteous people, who have not yet joined them, that is, who did not attend the lifetime of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) while he was teaching the Book and wisdom; and they will join them, and they are everyone among the Arabs and non-Arabs who did not attend the lifetime of the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 62, verses 5–8:

Explanation of the words:

حملوا التوراة (hamalū al-Tawrāh): i.e., they were charged with acting upon it in matters of belief, worship, judgment, manners and ethics.

ثم لم يحملوها (thumma lam yaḥmilūhā): i.e., they did not act upon what is in it. Among that is his description (ﷺ) and the command to believe in him; so they denied his description, distorted it, did not believe in him, and fought against him.

بئس مثل القوم الذين كذبوا بآيات الله (bi'sa mathal al-qawm alladhīna kadhdhabū bi-āyāt Allāh): i.e., those whose revelations confirm the Prophet (ﷺ). This is the parable which God struck for the Jews: like the donkey that carries books (asfār), i.e., books of knowledge, while it does not understand what is in them.

قل يا أيها الذين هادوا (qul yā ayyuhā alladhīna hādū): i.e., the Jews who adhere to Judaism.

إن زعمتم أنكم أولياء لله من دون الناس (in za'amtum annakum awliyā' li-Llāh min dūn al-nās): i.e., and that you are the sons of God and His beloved, and that Paradise is exclusively yours.

فتمنوا الموت إن كنتم صادقين (fa-tamannaw al-mawt in kuntum ṣādiqīn): i.e., if you are truthful that you are God's friends, then wish for death, preferring the Hereafter over this world; and the beginning of the Hereafter is death, so wish for it then.

بما قدمت أيديهم (bimā qaddamat aydīhim): i.e., because of what they have committed of disbelief and denial of the Prophet (ﷺ), they will not wish for it.

والله عليم بالظالمين (wa-Llāh 'alīm bi-l-ẓālimīn): i.e., the polytheists; and the implication of His knowledge of them is that He will recompense them for their wrongdoing with painful punishment.

تفرون منه (tafirrūna minhu): i.e., because you will never wish for it, and that is precisely fleeing from it.

فإنه ملاقيكم (fa-innahu mulāqīkum): i.e., wherever you turn, it will meet you face to face.

ثم تردون إلى عالم الغيب والشهادة (thumma turaddūna ilā 'ālim al-ghayb wa-l-shahādah): i.e., to God, Exalted, on the Day of Resurrection.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿The likeness of those who were charged with the Torah﴾: i.e., those among the Jews and Christians who were charged with acting upon it; ﴿then did not carry it﴾: i.e., then did not act upon what is in it of rulings and laws. Among that is their denial of the descriptions of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and the command to believe in him and follow him when he appeared. His saying: ﴿like the likeness of a donkey carrying books﴾: i.e., like a donkey that carries on its back books of beneficial knowledge, while it does not comprehend what it carries and does not know what good is on its back, because it neither reads nor understands. His saying: ﴿Evil is the likeness of the people who denied the signs of God﴾: i.e., those whose revelations confirm the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ); this is the parable which God struck for the People of the Book, Jews and Christians. His saying: ﴿And God does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾: and for this reason He did not guide them to Islam. Because of their immersion in wrongdoing, disbelief, evil and corruption, they were not worthy of God's guidance.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: O you who have become Jews﴾: i.e., say, O our Messenger, O you who were Jews, i.e., O you who claim to be upon the Jewish creed; ﴿if you claim that you are the allies of God, to the exclusion of other people﴾: since you claimed that you are the sons of God and His beloved, and that Paradise is yours to the exclusion of others, and other such claims of yours; ﴿then wish for death, if you are truthful in your claims﴾: since death is the path to the Abode of the Hereafter, so wish for it, that you may die and be relieved of the distresses and toils of this world.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they will never wish for it﴾: He, the All-Knowing, informs that they will never wish for it at any time, and God, Exalted, explained the cause of that in His saying: ﴿because of what their hands have sent forward﴾: of sins and offenses that necessitate punishment.

His saying: ﴿And God is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾: i.e., of the likes of these Jews, and He will recompense them for their wrongdoing with the punishment of Hellfire. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: Indeed, the death from which you flee﴾: i.e., say to them, O our Messenger, that the death from which you flee and which you do not wish for, out of fear and dread of it, will certainly meet you wherever you are; it will confront you face to face. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, who is God, Exalted, who knows what is hidden in the heavens and the earth, knows what His servants conceal and what they make public, what they reveal and what they hide. He will inform you of what you used to do and will recompense you with just recompense; indeed He is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

Guidance of the verses:

1- Condemnation of one who memorizes the Book of God but does not act upon what is in it.

2- Denunciation of wrongdoing and wrongdoers.

3- Clarification of the lies and deceit of the Jews in their claim to be God's allies and that Paradise is exclusively theirs.

4- Clarification that those with the most crimes are the people most fearful of death and most inclined to flee from it.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: O you who have become Jews﴾: i.e., say, O our Messenger, O you who were Jews, i.e., O you who claim to be upon the Jewish creed; ﴿if you claim that you are the allies of God, to the exclusion of other people﴾: since you claimed that you are the sons of God and His beloved, and that Paradise is yours to the exclusion of others, and other such claims of yours; ﴿then wish for death, if you are truthful in your claims﴾: since death is the path to the Abode of the Hereafter, so wish for it, that you may die and be relieved of the distresses and toils of this world.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they will never wish for it﴾: He, the All-Knowing, informs that they will never wish for it at any time, and God, Exalted, explained the cause of that in His saying: ﴿because of what their hands have sent forward﴾: of sins and offenses that necessitate punishment.

His saying: ﴿And God is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾: i.e., of the likes of these Jews, and He will recompense them for their wrongdoing with the punishment of Hellfire. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: Indeed, the death from which you flee﴾: i.e., say to them, O our Messenger, that the death from which you flee and which you do not wish for, out of fear and dread of it, will certainly meet you wherever you are; it will confront you face to face. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, who is God, Exalted, who knows what is hidden in the heavens and the earth, knows what His servants conceal and what they make public, what they reveal and what they hide. He will inform you of what you used to do and will recompense you with just recompense; indeed He is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

Guidance of the verses:

1- Condemnation of one who memorizes the Book of God but does not act upon what is in it.

2- Denunciation of wrongdoing and wrongdoers.

3- Clarification of the lies and deceit of the Jews in their claim to be God's allies and that Paradise is exclusively theirs.

4- Clarification that those with the most crimes are the people most fearful of death and most inclined to flee from it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 62, verses 9–11:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Idha nūdiya li-ṣ-ṣalāh﴾ (when the call is made for the prayer): i.e., when the muezzin gives the call to prayer while the imam is seated on the minbar (pulpit).

Min yawm al-jumu'ah (on the day of Friday): i.e., on the day of Friday, after the sun has passed its zenith.

Fa-s'aw ilā dhikr Allāh (then hasten to the remembrance of Allah): i.e., proceed to the prayer.

Wa-dharū al-bay' (and leave off trade): i.e., abandon it. If there is no selling, there is no buying.

Wa-btaghū min faḍl Allāh (and seek of Allah's bounty): i.e., seek provision from Allah, the Exalted, through striving and work.

Tuflihūn (you may prosper): i.e., you may be saved from the Fire and enter the Garden.

Infaḍḍū ilayhā (they dispersed toward it): i.e., toward the trade.

Wa-tarakūka qā'iman (and left you standing): i.e., on the minbar, delivering the Friday sermon.

Mā 'inda Allāh khayrun min al-lahwi wa-min al-tijārah (what is with Allah is better than amusement and trade): i.e., what Allah has of reward in the Hereafter is better than amusement and trade.

Wa-Allāhu khayru ar-rāziqīn (and Allah is the best of providers): i.e., so seek provision from Him through obedience and by following His guidance.

The meaning of the verses

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū﴾ (O you who have believed), i.e., O you who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger. ﴿Idhā nūdiya li-ṣ-ṣalāh min yawm al-jumu'ah﴾ (when the call is made for the prayer on the day of Friday), i.e., when the muezzin gives the call after the sun has passed its zenith on Friday and the imam is seated on the minbar. ﴿Fa-s'aw ilā dhikr Allāh﴾ (then hasten to the remembrance of Allah), i.e., proceed to the remembrance of Allah, which is the prayer and the sermon, for by them Allah, the Exalted, is remembered. And His saying ﴿wa-dharū al-bay'﴾ (and leave off trade), since it is the predominant of people's activities; otherwise all other activities must be halted and one must proceed to the prayer.

And His saying ﴿Dhālikum khayrun lakum in kuntum ta'lamūn﴾ (That is better for you, if you only knew), i.e., leaving off work, such as buying, selling and others, and proceeding to perform the Friday prayer and hear the sermon is better in reward and in outcome.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Fa-idhā quḍiyati aṣ-ṣalāh﴾ (Then when the prayer is concluded), i.e., performed and finished, ﴿fa-ntashirū fī al-arḍ﴾ (then disperse through the land), i.e., after the prayer ends you may scatter wherever you wish in the affairs of religion and of worldly life, ﴿wa-btaghū min faḍl Allāh﴾ (and seek of Allah's bounty), ﴿wa-dhkurū Allāh kathīrā﴾ (and remember Allah much), i.e., during your dispersal and your activities, remember Allah and do not forget Him, and remember Him much, ﴿la'allakum tuflihūn﴾ (that you may prosper), i.e., in hope of your success and triumph in this world and the Hereafter.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Wa-idhā ra'aw tijāratan aw lahwan infaḍḍū ilayhā wa-tarakūka qā'iman﴾ (And when they see a trade or amusement, they disperse toward it and leave you standing). This verse was revealed concerning a caravan of oil whose owner was Dihya ibn Khalifa al-Kalbi al-Ansari (may Allah be pleased with him), which arrived from Syria. It was the custom of the people of Madinah, when a trade caravan carrying provisions arrived, to welcome it with some amusement, such as beating drums and playing flutes. The caravan's arrival coincided with Friday while the people were in the mosque. When the prayer had ended and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came up onto the minbar to deliver the sermon—the sermon then being after the prayer, not before it as it became later—the people slipped away until only twelve men and a woman remained with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So this verse was revealed rebuking them for their going out and for leaving their Prophet delivering the sermon. In the form of severe reproach, He said: ﴿Wa-idhā ra'aw tijāratan aw lahwan infaḍḍū ilayhā﴾ (they disperse toward it), i.e., they went out toward it, ﴿wa-tarakūka﴾ (and leave you), O our Messenger, ﴿qā'iman﴾ (standing) on the minbar delivering the sermon. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Qul mā 'inda Allāhi khayrun mina al-lahwi wa-mina at-tijārah﴾ (Say: What is with Allah is better than amusement and trade), i.e., inform them, O our Prophet, that what Allah has of reward in the Hereafter is better than the amusement and trade for which you went out, ﴿wa-Allāhu khayru ar-rāziqīn﴾ (and Allah is the best of providers). So seek provision from Him by obeying Him and obeying His Messenger, and let not such a shameful act be repeated among you.

Otherwise, you may be exposed to a swift punishment that is not deferred.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation of the Friday prayer and the obligation to proceed to it at the second call, which takes place while the imam is on the minbar.

2- The prohibition of buying, selling and all other contracts once the muezzin begins the second call to prayer.

3- The encouragement to remember Allah and to remember Him often, for a person may buy, sell, work and labour while his tongue remains engaged in remembrance.

4- The number of worshippers with whom the Friday prayer is valid should not be less than twelve men, taking this from the incident in which the people dispersed from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was delivering the sermon, toward the caravan, until only twelve men remained.
